newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa improving but not yet out of danger.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa improving but not yet out of danger.

text.p: Mother Teresa was recovering slowly on Wednesday after life-saving heart surgery, but doctors said the 86-year-old nun's health was still at risk.
"Mother is improving but is still not out of danger," a panel of doctors treating the Roman Catholic missionary at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in a medical bulletin.
"She is cheerful," the statement said, adding that Mother Teresa had talked with sisters from her Missionaries of Charity order in the morning.
Earlier, clinic administrator S.K. Tiwari said the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner had a peaceful night in intensive care. "Mother Teresa had a good sleep," he said.
She took morning tea and later drank some fruit juice, the bulletin said.
The nun, revered for her life-long devotion to the poor, destitute and dying, has been suffering from an irregular heartbeat, bronchial pneumonia and weak kidneys.
She had surgery last week to clear two blocked arteries and had appeared to be recovering when longstanding kidney and lung problems resurfaced.
On Tuesday doctors said they were optimistic she would recover, but cautioned that she remained in critical condition and was still not out of danger.
They said she could take a long time to recuperate, and might never be as active as before.

"It may be months or years from now," Dr Tarun Praharaj, a member of the team, told reporters on Tuesday. He had been asked when Mother Teresa would recover from last week's surgery, her third coronary operation in five years.
Praharaj said she would go back to work at Missionaries of Charity once her heart and "other parameters" were declared satisfactory.
"But it will not be very, very active this time because we have to keep an eye on her health and monitor her parameters from time to time," he said. "It will not be as active as before."
Despite a series of health problems, Mother Teresa had kept up a seemingly tireless pace in her religious order before her latest illness and travelled widely.

Her Missionaries of Charity order runs 456 homes in 111 countries. The nun, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, had her first heart operation in the United States in 1991 and her second at the Birla centre in 1993.
